blocks.text: For this year’s edition of Paris Photo , IBASHO focuses on Japanese artists who live or lived outside of Japan and how that influenced their photographic practice. Their selection merges contemporary artists with classic vintage photography.
Miho Kajioka (FR) who has been living in Paris for four years, he has a renewed appreciation for Japanese culture, envisioned in unique works that she has created recently.
In her series ‘Ctrl Shift + J’ Sayuri Ichida (UK) explores the psychological impact of relocation and emigration.
Hideyuki Ishibashi (FR) made the waste heaps of Northern France the subject of his photographic experiments and Norio Takasugi’s (D) work is very much imbedded in German visual culture.
Naohiro Ninomiya (FR), who came to France in 1988 to become an artist, is inspired by both the French and the Japanese culture
Yumiko Izu (US/JP) created her series ‘Utsuroi’ (‘Transcience’) during the lockdown in upstate New York where she had been living for a long time, shortly before moving back to Japan.

Toshio Shibata (JP), after having studied Fine Art in Japan, started with photography in Ghent (B) where he studied at the Royal Art Academy in the 1970s. They will be exhibiting his earliest works made in Belgium, The Netherlands and Scotland.
Venice has been documented magically by Ikko Narahara (JP) when he travelled through Europe in the 1960s and revisited Venice thereafter in the 1980s. You will marvel at a selection of vintage works.
On Friday 13 November at 15:00 the artists Miho Kajioka, Sayuri Ichida and Norio Takasugi will be dedicating their recently published books at booth C17.
IBASHO @ Booth C17 with Miho Kajioka, Sayuri Ichida , Hideyuki Ishibashi , Norio Takasugi, Naohiro Ninomiya, Yumiko Izu , Toshio Shibata & Ikko Narahara.
Paris Photo November 12–15, 2026 | Grand Palais 1 p.m. – 8 p.m. (Sunday 7 p.m.) 3 avenue du Général Eisenhower 75008 Paris, France www.parisphoto.com
